title: Cross-host Linux and macOS effect evidence
description: Objective: collect production-surface effect conformance evidence on actual Linux and macOS hosts for every frozen platform boundary, bound to one exact source commit and distribution. Deliverable: host-native fault schedules/evidence receipts and a reproducible cross-host aggregation protocol. NOT in scope: implementing platform classifiers, running off-host fixtures as proof, or weakening Windows behavior. Hard dependencies: Linux boundary task-f01ef545b1554a2cb5df340ce78f6a5c, macOS boundary task-45d12ecfa6ae4938b23af28fe7876a44, doctor task-1cafc7f9fcdc4c9299860b6b1e38275d, and distribution packaging task-739879d0d1ce4a7ea4d1430688cdc4dc. Measured at HEAD 30458af on win32: tests/fault/linux/** and tests/fault/macos/** are absent; archived tasks-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275/e94b2055e281489ea9e97820919f6856 have no landing commits, and their reopen notes explicitly require live Linux/macOS hosts. Consumer: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93. Owned paths: tests/fault/linux/**, tests/fault/macos/**, cross-host evidence manifests/aggregation, and CI/host runner configuration only where approved.
definitionOfDone: On an actual Linux host and an actual macOS host, every hand-written PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES member runs crash-before/after activation and cancellation schedules against the production classifier/runner surface; each schedule asserts exact PROVEN/UNKNOWN code, layer, boundary, and a nonzero case count.

Each host record binds source commit, distribution manifest/digest, OS/kernel/arch, Node/pnpm/provider runtime closure, fixture/fault schedule digests, timestamps, and raw run receipts; unverifiable or mismatched bindings yield UNKNOWN and never PASS.
Linux and macOS receipts are canonical, immutable, independently verifiable, and aggregated without trusting caller-selected host claims; missing host evidence leaves only that OS row UNKNOWN.
No off-host test fixture, emulation label, or design claim is accepted as host proof; Windows stays a separate observation and is not weakened.
Host-native fault gates and the cross-host verifier exit 0, and task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 is recorded as the acceptance consumer.
taskRails: This task requires real Linux and macOS execution environments; do not claim completion from win32 alone.
Use production @moe/runner/platform and distribution/doctor surfaces, not test reimplementations.
Every refusal/unknown asserts stable code plus layer/boundary and every generated schedule asserts positive cardinality.
blockedReason:
Two measured causes. Full evidence in msg-60dd25ea3eb64357b31f0b86a0401a40 (general channel); this field caps at 2000.

CAUSE 1 — HARD DEPENDENCY UNMET. task-45d12ecfa6ae4938b23af28fe7876a44 "macOS platform observation boundary" is PLANNING, not DONE; the other three deps are COMPLETED. On disk at HEAD 7dbf9ba, packages/runner/src/platform/ has linux-boundary/linux-facts/linux-observation/platform-contract/platform-instant and windows/ — NO macos-* module. platform-contract.ts:38 freezes PLATFORM_LAYERS as ["PLATFORM_CONTRACT","PLATFORM_LINUX"]; no PLATFORM_MACOS. The production surface refuses darwin deliberately: platform-observation.test.ts:292 "refuses every boundary as PLATFORM_HOST_MISMATCH at PLATFORM_LINUX on a darwin host", :316 "macOS inherits no Linux verdict". On a real Mac all 7 PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES members return PLATFORM_HOST_MISMATCH by design, so DoD 1's "PROVEN/UNKNOWN against the production classifier" has nothing to prove against. Unsatisfiable, not merely hard.

CAUSE 2 — NO EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT. Session is win32; the repo has no CI config (.github/, .gitlab-ci.yml, azure-pipelines.yml, .circleci all absent), so no Linux or macOS runner exists to delegate to. Task rail 1 forbids win32-only completion; both archived predecessors (e87a7353, e94b2055) died on this wall with no landing commits.

TO UNBLOCK, in order:
1. Land task-45d12ecf — a macos observation module plus a PLATFORM_MACOS member in the frozen PLATFORM_LAYERS set.
2. Provide real hosts: attach Linux and macOS machines, or approve a CI config with linux+macos runners. Owned paths already say "CI/host runner configuration only where approved" — that approval is the human decision I cannot make.

I did not split the task. The authorable half (manifest schema, aggregation, UNKNOWN-on-missing-row) could land on win32, but carving it out unasked retires this id against a proof of shapes only. Say the word and I will file it. Windows untouched.
